applyImport.importScannedConfigOverwrite: Import the scanned config? This overwrites your current mode & network settings. You'll review and Apply afterward.
applyImport.importedReviewSettingsThen: Imported. Review the settings, then press Apply to regenerate configs and restart the stack.
applyNetwork.networkChangeAppliedConfirm: Network change applied — confirm to keep it before it reverts.
attachParams.fcs00290YsfReflector: e.g. FCS00290 or a YSF reflector
attachParams.modeCannotAttachCommitted: This mode cannot attach in the committed reframe tier.
attachPickerHTML.attachLocalModeGreyed: Attach a local mode (greyed-out modes can't, reason shown):
attachPickerHTML.attachModePairedPeer: Or attach a mode from a paired peer:
bm.dialSystemxTalkgroups4: Dial SystemX talkgroups with the 4 prefix (e.g. TG 3021 → 4003021 on TS2); routing is generated on the node.
bm.dialTgifTalkgroups5: Dial TGIF talkgroups with the 5 prefix (e.g. TG 31665 → 5031665 on TS2).
bm.privateLocksTxNode: Private locks TX to this node's own DMR ID; Public allows other DMR IDs through the hotspot.
busCard.busNeedsLeastTwo: A bus needs at least two attachments to hub traffic; add another mode before applying.
busCard.disabledItsAttachmentsAre: Disabled — its attachments are kept and return when you re-enable it.
busCard.name: Name
cal.applyingWritesSameNumber: Applying writes the same number to both RX and TX offset. A hotspot has one reference oscillator clocking both paths, so an error measured on receive is the same error transmitting — and the sweep can only measure the receive side without test equipment.
cal.nodeGoesOffAir: This node goes off the air while the sweep runs, and comes back on its own afterwards.
calCurve.curveIncompleteSweepRan: This curve is incomplete — the sweep ran out of time or was stopped. What is drawn was measured; what is missing was not.
calCurve.nothingWasDecodedAny: Nothing was decoded at any frequency. The radio was not transmitting, was not in DMR, or is outside the range the sweep covered.
callsign.keepTyping: Keep typing — the list is searched from {count} characters.
callsign.noMatch: No callsign in the list starts with that. You can still type one in full and add it.
callsign.noTable: This node has not downloaded the public ID list, so there is nothing to search. Type the callsign in full, or fetch the list from the Updates tab.
callsign.search: Search callsigns in the public ID list
callsign.showing: The first {shown}. Keep typing to narrow it.
callsign.typeToSearch: Type a callsign. The public ID list is searched as you go.
cancelSweep.stoppingSweepNodeComes: Stopping the sweep — the node comes back on the air by itself.
common.gatewayBlockedGeneric: This daemon is not started until the values above are set.
common.remoteGatewayAdvancedLeave: Remote gateway (advanced — leave off for local control)
confirmNetwork.browserDoesnTHold: This browser doesn't hold the confirm token for the pending change — confirm from the tab that applied it, or let it revert.
dash.eventlog.head: EVENT LOG
dash.eventlog.label: Event log entries
dash.gateways.empty: Gateway status appears here on a live node.
dash.gateways.head: GATEWAYS
dash.gateways.label: Gateway daemon status
dash.intro: Live activity for this node. Every row arrives over /api/events — no log scraping.
dash.lastheard.head: LAST HEARD
dash.lastheard.label: Last heard stations
dash.networks.head: NETWORKS
dash.networks.label: Network links
dash.onair.head: ON AIR
dash.onair.label: On air status
dash.title: Dashboard
detectModem.modemUseMmdvmHost: The modem is in use by MMDVM-Host, so it cannot answer.\n\nStop it, look for the modem, and start it again? This node will be off the air for a few seconds.
display.mmdvmHostBuildDisplay: This MMDVM-Host build is display-free — it renders status over MQTT and ignores these keys. They are carried for WPSD parity and for a clone running stock MMDVM-Host or driving a physical panel.
dmr.dmrIdInherited: This node logs in to DMR as {id} — the station DMR ID from General → Station Identity.
dmr.dmrIdNowhere: No DMR ID is set here or on the General tab, so DMR has nothing to log in with. Set the station DMR ID under General → Station Identity.
dmr.dmrIdOverridden: This node logs in to DMR as {id}. The station DMR ID ({station}) is unchanged, and the other gateways still use it.
dmr.hangTimerClamp: Leave a hang timer blank to keep using the global mode hang from the General tab. Call hold latches the talkgroup you last heard so a reply keys back to it. MMDVM-Host clamps TX hang down to the smaller of the two mode hangs, then clamps call hold down to TX hang, so an oversized value is silently reduced rather than rejected.
dmr.messageRelayNote: Lets this node send and receive DMR text messages, by relaying the loopback between MMDVM-Host and DMRGateway. Off by default: with it on, waypointd carries every DMR frame, so restarting it costs a few seconds of DMR. Leave it off if you do not use messaging.
dmr.talkerAliasNote: Names a caller on the receiving radio's screen instead of a bare DMR ID, on calls coming in from the network. The names come from your Phonebook — a caller who isn't in it is sent no alias and shows as before. Off by default.
dstar.ref001CBlankNone: e.g. REF001 C — blank for none
dstar.reflectorListNotLoaded: Reflector list not loaded yet (fetched from the pinned D-Star register on a schedule). You can still type a reflector above.
expert.rawIniEditingPower: Raw INI editing and power controls land in a later slice. Config now lives in the store; the INIs are regenerated on Apply — waypoint#29.
firmware.firmwareDownloadedSignedRelease: Firmware is downloaded from a signed release and its signature checked before a byte reaches the modem. On a GPIO board the bootloader lives in the chip and cannot be erased, so an interrupted flash is recoverable by trying again.
firmware.nodeAirFlashingStops: This node is on the air. Flashing stops MMDVM-Host, writes the modem, and starts it again — about a minute of downtime. You will be asked to confirm.
firmware.nothingAnsweredDetectionSo: Nothing answered detection, so this is using the board and port already configured on this node. That is the normal state after an interrupted flash — the modem cannot run its firmware, so it cannot answer — and it is exactly when flashing has to still work. The bootloader is in the chip and answers regardless.
firmware.pickImageMatchesOscillator: Pick the image that matches the oscillator fitted to your board. Getting this wrong does not fail loudly — the node comes up and transmits off frequency — which is why Waypoint will not choose for you.
firmware.waypointWillNotChoose: Waypoint will not choose this for you.
fixUART.freeGpioSerialPort: Free the GPIO serial port for the modem?\n\nThis edits config.txt and cmdline.txt on the boot partition and masks the serial login service. The node must be rebooted afterwards.
fixUART.gpioSerialPortWas: The GPIO serial port was already free.
fixUART.hostHasNoRaspberry: This host has no Raspberry Pi boot partition, so there is no GPIO serial port to free.
flashFirmware.flashingDoNotPower: Flashing — do not power the node off.
gateways.noBusesYetBus: No buses yet. A bus lets its attached modes hear each other (DMR ⇄ YSF ⇄ NXDN), with IDs/talkgroups translated per side. Create one, then attach two or more modes.
gateways.oldPerModeBridges: The old per-mode bridges (YSF2DMR, DMR2YSF, YSF2NXDN, DMR2NXDN, NXDN2DMR) are retired. Migration seeds a bus from whatever you had configured — your saved bridge settings are preserved either way, migration only adds a bus, it never deletes anything.
general.callsignHelp: Choosing a callsign from the list fills in the DMR ID below. A callsign the list does not carry is fine — type it and enter the ID yourself.
general.donTTypePort: Don't type the port and board in by hand — the Hardware tab asks the modem what it is and fills all of this in.
general.hotspotBoardIgnoresEvery: A hotspot board ignores every setting in this card — its firmware never reads them. They are for full-size MMDVM repeater boards.
general.leaveBlankFollowTx: Leave blank to follow TX Level, which is what almost every node wants. M17 has no separate level — MMDVM-Host has no key for one, so it always follows TX Level.
general.measureTheseRatherThan: Measure these rather than guess them — the Hardware tab sweeps for the offset with your radio and writes the answer here.
hardware.adoptingWritesPortLine: Adopting writes the port, line speed, board and reference oscillator into this node's configuration. An oscillator the firmware did not actually report is never written — a reference frequency guessed wrong detunes the radio.
hardware.boardSittingItsBootloader: A board is sitting in its bootloader
hardware.editsConfigTxtCmdline: This edits config.txt and cmdline.txt on the boot partition and masks the serial login service. Your own settings in those files are left alone. The node must be rebooted for it to take effect.
hardware.gpioSerialPortFree: The GPIO serial port is free for a modem: the UART is on, Bluetooth is not holding it, and no login console is attached.
hardware.hatFittedNodeCannot: A hat fitted to this node cannot be heard. On stock Raspberry Pi OS the serial port a GPIO modem needs is switched off, owned by the onboard Bluetooth controller, or occupied by a login console — the board is electrically fine and completely silent.
hardware.modemAnsweredButIts: This modem answered, but its identity does not match any board Waypoint knows. Its port is still worth adopting; leave the board as-is or pick the closest match.
hardware.nodeHasNotLooked: This node has not looked for a modem yet. Detect asks every serial port that could plausibly be a modem what is on the end of it — it sends one three-byte version request and nothing else.
hardware.nodeModemDisagree: THIS NODE AND THIS MODEM DISAGREE
hardware.nothingAdoptUntilModem: Nothing to adopt until a modem has been found.
hardware.portsAlreadyClaimedSomething: Ports already claimed for something else — a Nextion display, above all — are left alone rather than probed.
hardware.theseAreConfigurationsProduce: These are configurations that produce a node which starts, reports itself healthy, and does not work on the air. Nothing here blocks Apply — the modem may be the thing that is wrong.
help.display.hd44780_i2c_addr: I2C address of the panel's PCF8574 backpack, in hex. 0x27 and 0x3F cover most modules.
help.display.hd44780_rows: Character rows on the panel — 2 and 4 are the common sizes.
help.display.port: Where the display is attached — the modem's own pass-through, or a named serial device. None leaves the node headless, which is the normal Waypoint setup.
help.dmr.beacons: Sends the DMR Roaming Beacon, which lets radios that support roaming discover this node and move to it automatically.
help.dmr.color_code: DMR's equivalent of a CTCSS tone: a number 0–15 that must match at both ends before traffic is accepted. It keeps neighbouring systems on the same frequency from hearing each other. Most hotspots use 1.
help.dmr.dump_ta_data: Logs Talker Alias data — the sending operator's name and callsign carried alongside voice. Diagnostic; it adds noise to the log without changing what is transmitted.
help.dmr.embedded_lc_only: Sends only the Link Control data embedded in DMR voice bursts, leaving out the separate LC data burst. Some networks and repeaters expect this; leave it off unless yours has told you otherwise. Renders to [DMR] EmbeddedLCOnly.
help.dmr.id: Optional override. Leave blank and the node uses the DMR ID from General → Station Identity. Set it only when this node must log in to DMR with a different ID from the one the other gateways use — a separate hotspot ID, for instance.
help.dmr.self_only: Private accepts traffic only from your own DMR ID, so nobody else can key the node. Public accepts any DMR ID. Private is the usual choice for a personal hotspot. Renders to [DMR] SelfOnly.
help.dmrnet.slot1: DMR carries two independent timeslots on one frequency. Turning slot 1 on lets it carry traffic. On a simplex hotspot both slots are usually enabled and the network decides which to use.
help.dmrnet.slot2: The second DMR timeslot. Most talkgroup traffic on BrandMeister arrives on slot 2, so leaving this off will make the node look silent.
help.dstar.module: The single band letter this node identifies as, e.g. B for 70cm or C for 2m. It must match the module your radio calls, and the Band configured in the D-Star gateway.
help.dstar.remote_gateway: Hands network control to a gateway running elsewhere. Leave this off when the node runs its own D-Star gateway, which is the normal setup.
help.dstar.self_only: Accept traffic only from your own callsign, so nobody else can key the node.
help.dstargw.dcs: Enable the DCS reflector protocol (the DCS reflectors).
help.dstargw.dextra: Enable the DExtra reflector protocol (the XRF reflectors).
help.dstargw.dplus: Enable the DPlus reflector protocol (the REF reflectors). DPlus requires registration with a US Trust server.
help.dstargw.dplus_login: Callsign used to authenticate to DPlus reflectors — normally your own, and it must be registered with the US Trust system.
help.dstargw.ircddb_hostname: The ircDDB server that resolves callsigns to routes, e.g. rr.openquad.net. This is what makes callsign routing work.
help.dstargw.ircddb_password: Password issued when you registered with the ircDDB network. Stored on the node and never shown again.
help.dstargw.ircddb_username: Your callsign as registered with the ircDDB network. It must be registered there before routing will work.
help.dstargw.reflector: The reflector this node links to when it starts, e.g. REF001 C. Leave blank to start unlinked.
help.dstargw.reflector_reconnect: Whether the node returns to its startup reflector after a period of inactivity, and how long it waits. Never leaves it wherever the last user linked it.
help.dstargw.xlx: Enable XLX reflectors, which bridge D-Star with other modes.
help.fm.access_mode: How a transmission is allowed to open the repeater — on carrier alone, or only with the correct CTCSS tone. Requiring the tone stops unrelated signals keying the node.
help.fm.ctcss: The sub-audible access tone in Hz, e.g. 88.5. Your radio must send the same tone before the node will repeat you.
help.fm.ext_audio_boost: Gain applied to audio arriving from the network. Raise it if the network sounds quiet on the air.
help.fm.kerchunk_time: Seconds you must hold a transmission before the node responds, which stops brief “kerchunks” keying it. 0 turns it off.
help.fm.rf_audio_boost: Gain applied to audio arriving over the air. Raise it if you sound quiet to the network.
help.fm.timeout: Maximum seconds of continuous transmission before the node stops keying — the classic repeater timer that stops a stuck mic holding the channel.
help.general.callsign: Your licensed callsign. It identifies this node on every network it connects to, and is what other operators see in last-heard lists. Changing it re-registers the node with its gateways on Apply.
help.general.duplex: Simplex transmits and receives on one frequency, one at a time — the normal hotspot arrangement. Duplex uses separate RX and TX frequencies and needs hardware that supports it. Setting this wrong stops the node passing traffic.
help.general.id: Your DMR ID (sometimes called a CCS7 ID) — the numeric identity issued with your callsign by radioid.net. This is the node-wide default: DMR, and the YSF, P25, NXDN and M17 gateways, all log in with it unless a mode overrides it.
help.general.location: Free text shown to other operators and on network dashboards, e.g. “Kansas City, MO”. Cosmetic — nothing routes on it.
help.general.power: Transmit power in watts, as reported to the network. This is a declaration, not a control — it tells other operators what you are running, it does not change what the radio actually transmits.
help.general.url: A link to this node's public dashboard, published to networks that show one. Leave blank if the node is not reachable from the internet.
help.history.retention_days: How many days of last-heard and event history the node keeps on disk. 0 keeps it forever. Older events are pruned nightly; a longer window uses more SD-card space.
help.lcd.activity_interrupt: Let radio activity take over the panel as it happens, instead of waiting for the page rotation to come round.
help.lcd.enabled: Drive a physically attached HD44780 character panel. Off by default — the node stays headless and reports status over MQTT instead.
help.lcd.i2c_address: I2C address of the panel's backpack, in hex — commonly 0x27 or 0x3F.
help.lcd.i2c_bus: I2C device the panel is wired to. /dev/i2c-1 is the header bus on every Pi since the B+.
help.lcd.linger_secs: Seconds a page stays on the panel before the next one rotates in.
help.lcd.scroll_speed: How fast text longer than the panel scrolls across it.
help.m17.allow_encryption: Pass encrypted M17 frames through the node. Encrypted transmissions are prohibited on amateur bands in most countries — leave this off unless you are certain of your local rules.
help.m17.can: Channel Access Number — M17's equivalent of a CTCSS tone, 0–15. It must match at both ends. 0 is the common default.
help.m17.self_only: Accept traffic only from your own callsign.
help.m17gw.hang_time: Seconds of silence before the node reverts to its startup reflector.
help.m17gw.revert: Return to the startup reflector after the hang time below.
help.m17gw.startup: The reflector and module this node links to when it starts, e.g. M17-M17 C. Leave blank to start unlinked.
help.m17gw.suffix: A short suffix distinguishing several M17 nodes running on one callsign.
help.m17gw.voice: Play spoken announcements when the node links or unlinks.
help.modem.board: Which modem board is fitted. Detection reads the board family off the wire, but several products ship the same firmware — a JumboSpot reports as an MMDVM_HS_Hat — so where the identity string cannot tell them apart, this is where you say which one you have. It changes no generated config; it is what lets Waypoint refuse duplex on a board with one radio, and warn when a saved profile came from a differently-tuned board.
help.modem.dmr_delay: Fine timing adjustment for DMR slot alignment on a duplex repeater, in bits. Leave at 0 unless a repeater is losing slot sync.
help.modem.dmr_tx_level: Per-mode transmit level override for DMR. Blank follows TX Level.
help.modem.dstar_tx_level: Per-mode transmit level override for D-Star. Blank follows TX Level, which is what almost every node should do — these exist for a radio whose deviation differs between modes.
help.modem.fm_tx_level: Per-mode transmit level override for analog FM. Blank follows TX Level.
help.modem.nxdn_tx_level: Per-mode transmit level override for NXDN. Blank follows TX Level.
help.modem.p25_tx_level: Per-mode transmit level override for P25. Blank follows TX Level.
help.modem.pocsag_tx_level: Per-mode transmit level override for POCSAG paging. Blank follows TX Level.
help.modem.port: Serial device the MMDVM modem appears as — /dev/ttyAMA0 for a GPIO hat, /dev/ttyACM0 for most USB boards. Use Detect on the Hardware tab rather than typing it: detection asks each candidate port what is on the end of it, so a renumbered USB device is found rather than guessed at.
help.modem.ptt_invert: Whether the PTT line is active-low rather than active-high. Wrong, and the repeater either never keys or never stops. A hotspot ignores this.
help.modem.rf_level: RF output power of a hotspot's ADF7021, 0–100%. A hotspot is a milliwatt-class transmitter — this is the difference between reaching the far side of the house and the far side of the room, not a power amplifier control.
help.modem.rssi_mapping_file: Path to a file mapping the modem's raw RSSI counts to dBm, so received signal strengths are reported in real units. Producing one needs a calibrated signal generator; the default path is where the stack looks for it.
help.modem.rx_dc_offset: DC bias on the receive path, −128 to 127, used to centre the waveform on a full-size MMDVM. A hotspot ignores this entirely.
help.modem.rx_freq_hz: The frequency this node listens on — the frequency your radio transmits to. On a simplex hotspot it matches the TX frequency. Check your national band plan before choosing one.
help.modem.rx_invert: Whether the received signal arrives inverted. A full-size MMDVM can be asked directly — it reports inversion in its calibration replies — which is the one analog setting that does not need test equipment. A hotspot ignores this.
help.modem.rx_level: How hard the modem drives its own receive path, 0–100%. On a hotspot this does nothing — the firmware does not read it. On a repeater board it is set so the received waveform fills the range without clipping.
help.modem.rx_offset: Correction in Hz applied to the receive frequency, compensating for crystal error in the modem. Leave at 0 until you have measured the error — this is calibration, not tuning.
help.modem.tcxo_hz: The modem's reference oscillator, in Hz — 12288000 (12.288 MHz) or 14745600 (14.7456 MHz). Firmware from the 1.5 era onwards reports it, and Detect fills this in from what the modem said. Get it wrong and the radio is detuned rather than broken, which is why nothing here ever guesses one.
help.modem.tx_dc_offset: DC bias on the transmit path, −128 to 127. A hotspot ignores this entirely.
help.modem.tx_freq_hz: The frequency this node transmits on — the frequency your radio listens to. On a simplex hotspot it matches the RX frequency.
help.modem.tx_invert: Whether the transmit signal is inverted before it reaches the radio. Depends on how the radio's modulator is wired. A hotspot ignores this.
help.modem.tx_level: Transmit level, 0–100%. On a hotspot this is the deviation of the 4FSK signal it generates; on a repeater board it drives the radio's audio input and is set for 2.75 kHz deviation with a deviation meter.
help.modem.tx_offset: Correction in Hz applied to the transmit frequency, compensating for crystal error in the modem. Leave at 0 until you have measured the error. On a hotspot one oscillator clocks both paths, so this is normally the same number as the RX offset.
help.modem.uart_speed: Line speed between the host and the modem. 115200 is the MMDVM_HS family's default and is almost always right; Detect fills in whichever speed the modem actually answered on.
help.modem.ysf_tx_level: Per-mode transmit level override for System Fusion. Blank follows TX Level.
help.modes.dmr: Digital Mobile Radio — the most widely used amateur digital mode, with talkgroups carried over networks like BrandMeister and TGIF.
help.modes.dstar: Icom's D-Star, routing through reflectors and callsign-based gateways.
help.modes.fm: Plain analog FM. It has no gateway of its own — the node simply repeats it.
help.modes.m17: M17 — a fully open, patent-free digital voice mode built on Codec2.
help.modes.nxdn: NXDN, connecting to NXDN reflectors by talkgroup.
help.modes.p25: APCO P25 Phase 1, connecting to P25 reflectors by talkgroup.
help.modes.pocsag: POCSAG paging over DAPNET. Transmits pages rather than voice.
help.modes.ysf: Yaesu System Fusion (C4FM), connecting to YSF reflectors and FCS rooms.
help.mqtt.auth: Whether the daemons log in to the broker. Leave this off for the normal setup, where mosquitto listens only on localhost and there is nothing to authenticate against. Turn it on if you have pointed this node at a broker that requires credentials.
help.mqtt.bus_prefix: Topic root for mode-bus events. The bus daemons publish here and the dashboard consumes it; both are rewritten on Apply, so the badges keep working across the change.
help.mqtt.host: Where the MQTT broker lives. Every daemon on this node publishes to it and the dashboard reads from it, so this is the one address they all have to agree on. Normally 127.0.0.1 — mosquitto runs on the node itself and is not exposed to the network.
help.mqtt.name: MMDVM-Host's [MQTT] Name, which is the root of every topic the modem publishes (<name>/json, <name>/log). The dashboard subscribes to the same value, so changing it here moves both together. Only change this if you run two nodes against one broker and need to tell them apart.
help.mqtt.password: Broker password. Stored on the node and never shown again — leave the field blank to keep the one already saved.
help.mqtt.port: Broker TCP port. 1883 is plain MQTT (the default for a local broker); 8883 is the conventional TLS port.
help.mqtt.status_prefix: Topic root for the normalized status this dashboard republishes for Home Assistant and other consumers. Change it only to avoid a collision with something else on a shared broker — Home Assistant discovery follows it automatically.
help.mqtt.username: Broker username, sent only when authentication is on.
help.nxdn.ran: Radio Access Number — NXDN's equivalent of a CTCSS tone, 0–63. It must match at both ends. 1 is the common default.
help.nxdn.remote_gateway: Hands network control to a gateway running elsewhere. Leave off when the node runs its own NXDN gateway.
help.nxdn.self_only: Accept traffic only from your own ID.
help.nxdngw.net_hang_time: Seconds the node stays on a talkgroup after network traffic stops.
help.nxdngw.rf_hang_time: Seconds the node stays on a talkgroup after you stop transmitting.
help.nxdngw.static: Talkgroups the node links to at startup and stays on. Leave blank to start unlinked.
help.nxdngw.voice: Play spoken announcements when the node links or unlinks.
help.p25.nac: Network Access Code — P25's equivalent of a CTCSS tone, written in hex. It must match at both ends. 293 is the common default.
help.p25.override_uid_check: Skip validation of the source ID on incoming traffic. Leave off unless a radio you trust is being rejected.
help.p25.remote_gateway: Hands network control to a gateway running elsewhere. Leave off when the node runs its own P25 gateway.
help.p25.self_only: Accept traffic only from your own ID.
help.p25gw.net_hang_time: Seconds the node stays on a talkgroup after network traffic stops.
help.p25gw.rf_hang_time: Seconds the node stays on a talkgroup after you stop transmitting.
help.p25gw.static: Talkgroups the node links to at startup and stays on. Leave blank to start unlinked.
help.p25gw.voice: Play spoken announcements when the node links or unlinks.
help.pocsag.auth_key: The AuthKey issued by the DAPNET portal for your callsign. Stored on the node and never shown again.
help.pocsag.blacklist: Never transmit pages for these RICs, even when the server sends them.
help.pocsag.callsign: The callsign this node authenticates to DAPNET with. It must be registered with DAPNET separately from your radio licence.
help.pocsag.frequency: The paging transmit frequency in Hz. Amateur paging uses specific national allocations — check yours before transmitting.
help.pocsag.server: DAPNET server this node fetches pages from, e.g. dapnet.afu.rwth-aachen.de.
help.pocsag.whitelist: Only transmit pages for these RICs (pager addresses). Leave blank to transmit everything the server sends.
help.station_id.callsign: Identify with a different callsign from your station callsign. Leave blank to track General → Callsign automatically.
help.station_id.enable: Keys your callsign in Morse at a fixed interval, so the node identifies itself without you doing anything. Most licences require periodic identification — in the US, every 10 minutes (§97.119).
help.station_id.time_mins: Minutes between identifications. Set this to your licence's requirement or shorter — 10 minutes in the US. Identification is sent between transmissions, never during one.
help.station_id.tx_level: Loudness of the Morse identification, as a percentage of full deviation. Raise it if the ID is hard to copy, lower it if it is jarring next to voice traffic.
help.update.allow_unrevertable: Allow an update to go ahead even when the versions you are running are no longer in the repository, so it could not be undone if it went wrong. Normally the node refuses such an update and stays where it is. Turn this on only to get a node moving that would otherwise be stuck, and turn it back off afterwards.
help.update.auto_apply: Install updates automatically when they are found. Updates are health-checked after installing, and roll themselves back if the modem does not come back up.
help.update.channel: Which stream of releases this node follows. Stable is the tested one; the others get changes earlier and with more risk.
help.update.check_enabled: Check the signed Waypoint apt repository for new versions. Turning this off means the node never contacts the update server — you will need to check by hand.
help.update.quiet_window: A daily window during which updates are not installed, so a restart never lands in the middle of your regular operating time.
help.ysf.low_deviation: Use narrow deviation, matching radios set to the narrow C4FM setting. Getting this wrong gives distorted or unreadable audio rather than silence.
help.ysf.mode_hang: Seconds the node stays in YSF after traffic stops, before it will switch to another mode. Longer values favour continuing a YSF conversation over letting another mode in.
help.ysf.remote_gateway: Hands network control to a gateway running elsewhere. Leave off when the node runs its own YSF gateway.
help.ysf.self_only: Accept traffic only from your own callsign.
help.ysf.tx_hang: Seconds the transmitter stays keyed after a transmission ends, so a quick reply does not have to re-open the link.
help.ysfgw.aprs: Publish position and status to the APRS network.
help.ysfgw.enable_dgid: Use DG-ID routing, which maps DG-ID numbers set on the radio to different reflectors.
help.ysfgw.fcs_network: Connect to the FCS room network. FCS rooms are a separate system from YSF reflectors, and can be enabled alongside them.
help.ysfgw.inactivity_timeout: Minutes of silence before the node reverts to its startup reflector. 0 disables the revert.
help.ysfgw.revert: Return to the startup reflector after the inactivity timeout below.
help.ysfgw.startup: The YSF reflector or FCS room this node links to when it starts. Leave blank to start unlinked.
help.ysfgw.suffix: A short suffix appended to the callsign sent to the network, distinguishing several nodes running on one callsign.
help.ysfgw.upper_hostfiles: Fetch reflector host lists from the alternate upstream source.
help.ysfgw.wiresx_passthrough: Pass Wires-X commands from the radio through to the network, so you can change reflectors from the radio's own menu instead of this page.
help.ysfgw.ycs_network: Connect to YCS servers, which add per-talkgroup routing on top of YSF.
help.ysfgw.ysf_network: Connect to the YSF reflector network.
hostlistNote.listCouldNotDownloaded: This list could not be downloaded, so the picker below is empty.
hostlistNote.listMayOutDate: This list may be out of date.
hostlistNote.showingListShippedWaypoint: Showing the list that shipped with Waypoint.
import.copyIncumbentSEtc: Copy the incumbent's /etc/mmdvmhost, /etc/dmrgateway and other gateway config files off the old card, or mount the card and give its path. Nothing is written until you press Import.
importProfile.profileNameAlreadyExists: A profile with that name already exists. Overwrite it?
importReport.everythingFoundMapsWaypoint: Everything found maps to Waypoint — nothing left behind.
importReport.overwritesCurrentModeAmp: Overwrites your current mode & network config with the scanned values. Passwords carry over from the card; review, then
importReport.theseIncumbentFeaturesAren: These incumbent features aren't modeled yet — reconfigure them in Waypoint after importing.
ipv4Editor.dhcpListingDnsServers: With DHCP, listing DNS servers here replaces the ones the DHCP server hands out (ignore-auto-dns).
lcd.driverDisabledPagesAre: The driver is disabled — pages are saved but nothing is drawn until you enable it above.
lcd.linesFillTokensE: Lines fill in from {tokens} — e.g. {callsign}, {status}, {source}. A line wider than the panel scrolls; characters outside plain ASCII show as ?. A page may have at most as many lines as the panel has rows.
lcd.noPagesYetAdd: No pages yet — add one to show something on the panel.
lcd.pageInterruptTitle: Take over the panel on TX/RX, then resume rotation
lcd.token.ber: Bit-error rate of the last transmission
lcd.warnUnknownToken: ⚠ Unknown token: {tokens} — check spelling; unknown tokens render blank.
lcd.warnUnknownTokens: ⚠ Unknown tokens: {tokens} — check spelling; unknown tokens render blank.
lcdDetect.adoptWritesBusAddress: Using this panel writes its bus and address into the LCD settings and switches the driver on. Pages, rows and columns are left alone — a probe can tell Waypoint where a panel is, not how big it is.
lcdDetect.alreadyDriving: This is the panel Waypoint is driving.
lcdDetect.neverLooked: This node has not looked for a character panel yet. Look for a panel reads one byte from each address a PCF8574 backpack can occupy, and nothing else on the bus is touched.
lcdDetect.noneBanner: No panel answered on any I2C bus.
lcdDetect.nothingAnswered: Nothing answered on the I2C bus, last looked {when}. On Raspberry Pi OS the bus is off until it is enabled, so a wired panel with I2C disabled looks exactly like no panel at all.
lcdDetect.saveOrDiscardFirst: Save or discard your LCD changes first — using the detected panel rewrites this section.
m17.m17M17CBlank: e.g. M17-M17 C — blank for none
m17.reflectorListNotLoaded: Reflector list not loaded yet (fetched from the M17 register on a schedule). You can still type a reflector above.
m17.revertStartupReflectorAfter: Revert to startup reflector after inactivity
messages.err.failed: The node could not queue that.
messages.err.long: That is longer than a DMR text message can carry.
messages.intro: Send a text message to a radio over this node’s own RF, and see the ones that cross it. Nothing here is public.
messages.log.head: MESSAGES
messages.log.label: Text messages
messages.prereq: The receiving radio must have its channel set to M-SMS format with APRS Receive switched OFF. Anytone and BTECH firmware treats APRS receive and SMS as mutually exclusive: with it on, the radio decodes the message, lights up, and discards it.
messages.relay.hint: The DMR message relay is switched off, so nothing can be transmitted. Turn it on in Settings and press Apply.
messages.send.head: SEND
messages.sent.queued: Queued — waiting for a clear channel.
messages.title: Messages
modem.hostBlocked: MMDVM-Host is not started until these are set. Without a modem port there is nothing for it to open, at zero the modem refuses the frequency and the host stops, and a station may not transmit without a callsign and ID. Every mode depends on it, so nothing is on the air until this is filled in.
modes.turnModeHaveMmdvm: Turn a mode on to have MMDVM-Host handle it. Toggling one restarts the stack on Apply.
netHostCard.appliesImmediatelyHostnameTi: Applies immediately (hostname, timezone & NTP can't strand the node).
netScanSection.noNetworksFoundYet: No networks found yet — press Rescan, or enter an SSID above for a hidden network.
netStatusSection.noLiveEthernetWi: No live Ethernet or Wi-Fi interfaces reported.
netVlanCard.noVlansAddOne: No VLANs. Add one to put a tagged interface on a parent device.
network.appliesThroughConfirmRevert: Applies through confirm-or-revert — you'll get a countdown to keep the change before it auto-reverts.
network.editingHereWritesStore: Editing here writes the store and, on Apply Network, renders NetworkManager keyfiles behind a confirm-or-revert guard so a bad change can't strand the node. Waypoint only manages its own waypoint-* profiles; your hand-made connections are never touched.
notify.fromHelp: The address notifications are sent from. Many providers require this to match the account you sign in with.
notify.parkedHelp: Notifications that could not be delivered after several tries. They are not retried again, and they stay here until the problem is fixed.
notify.parkedTable: Notifications that could not be delivered
notify.passwordHelp: Stored on this node and never shown again. Leave blank to keep the current one.
notify.testFailed: Could not queue the test message.
notify.testHelp: Queues a test message. Delivery happens in the background, so nothing here waits on your mail server — if it does not arrive, the reason appears in the list beside this one.
notify.testNoAddresses: No Phonebook entry has an email address yet, so there is nowhere to send a test. Add one on the Phonebook tab.
notify.testPickSomebody: Choose who to send the test to.
notify.tlsHelp: By default the connection must be encrypted, and sending is refused if the server will not. Only relax that for a mail server on your own network.
nxdn.talkgroupListNotLoaded: Talkgroup list not loaded yet (fetched from the NXDN register on a schedule). You can still type talkgroup numbers above.
overrides.dropInsLine: Override drop-ins live under {dir} and host-file hooks under {prepend} · {append}. They merge last into the generated files and are never touched by an update ({issue}).
overrides.noOverridesActiveGenerated: No overrides active — the generated configuration is exactly what the store renders.
p25.talkgroupListNotLoaded: Talkgroup list not loaded yet (fetched from the P25 register on a schedule). You can still type talkgroup numbers above.
peerModal.sLanPeersScreen: 's LAN Peers screen, then confirm here.
peersCard.noPairedPeersYet: No paired peers yet. Discover a node or add one by host:port, then pair.
peersCard.noPeersFoundLan: No peers found on the LAN. Add one by host:port below (mDNS may be filtered on your network).
peersCard.pairWaypointNodesLan: Pair Waypoint nodes on your LAN so a bus can span them. Pairing shows a short code on both screens — enter it to confirm; the certificate fingerprint is shown for out-of-band verification.
pending.settingsArenTWired: settings aren't wired yet — a later slice of the configuration store (
phonebook.callsignHelp: Choosing a callsign from the list fills in the DMR ID and name, and the entry then follows the public list if the callsign is reissued. A callsign the list does not carry is fine — type it and fill in the rest yourself.
phonebook.confirmDelete: Remove this entry from the phonebook?
phonebook.confirmRevoke: Revoke the login for {username}? They are signed out everywhere immediately. Their phonebook entry stays.
phonebook.emailHelp: Email is only ever shown here, on this signed-in page. It appears on no public page and in no log.
phonebook.empty: No entries yet. Add the first one using the form beside this list.
phonebook.findNoTable: This node has not downloaded the public ID database yet. Check for updates on the Updates tab, then try again.
phonebook.findNotListed: That DMR ID is no longer in the public list.
phonebook.grantHelp: You choose the first password and read it to them. They must set their own before anything else on this node will open to them.
phonebook.hasAccount: This entry cannot be removed while somebody signs in as it — revoke this entry's login first.
phonebook.importEmailFailed: The entry was added from the public list, but its email address could not be saved. Add it with Edit.
phonebook.lastAdmin: This is the only administrator. Give somebody else the administrator role first, or this node would be left with nobody who can manage it.
phonebook.listHelp: Changes here save immediately. These are not radio settings, so nothing is applied and no daemon restarts.
phonebook.mustRotateHelp: This account is still using the password you chose for it. Until they set their own, it can reach nothing but the password screen.
phonebook.rotateHelp: The password you set here is one two people know. They are asked to replace it the first time they sign in.
phonebook.trackedHelp: Added from the public DMR ID database. The callsign and name are refreshed from it automatically; edit either one and this entry becomes yours and stops being refreshed.
pocsag.dapnetgatewayWillNotConnect: DAPNETGateway will not connect until a valid AuthKey is set (get one from the DAPNET web portal). Leave whitelist/blacklist blank to pass all RICs.
pocsag.gatewayBlockedAuthKey: POCSAG is enabled but no DAPNET AuthKey is set, so DAPNETGateway is not started — it would exit immediately and restart in a loop. Get an AuthKey from the DAPNET web portal, set it above, and apply. Everything else about POCSAG is already configured; nothing else is wrong.
profiles.activatingProfileWritesIts: Activating a profile writes its saved modes & networks and restarts the stack — the same as an Apply. Exported files have passwords removed; on import you re-enter any that are needed (or the target node keeps its own). Identity and calibration are never in a profile (RFC-0006).
profiles.noProfilesYetConfigure: No profiles yet. Configure your modes and networks, then Save current setup to capture this configuration as a profile you can switch back to.
publicview.customHtmlWarning: Advanced. This runs in an isolated frame that cannot reach the rest of the page or your session — but you own what you paste here.
publicview.enabledHelp: Anyone who can reach this node will be able to see the page.
publicview.linkHelp: Only http:// and https:// addresses are accepted.
publicview.logoHelp: PNG or JPEG, up to 1 MB. The image is re-encoded here, which removes any location and camera information the file was carrying.
publicview.offNote: Off. Every public address answers "not found" — a visitor cannot tell this node from one that never had the feature. Configure what you want shown first, then switch it on.
publicview.onNote: The public page is live at
publicview.retentionHelp: How far back the public page looks, 1 to 168 hours. This only limits what is shown — nothing is deleted, and your own history is unaffected.
publicview.showGridHelp: Off by default. This is the one field that says where you are.
publicview.suppressHelp: Callsigns here never appear in the public last-heard list, the counters or the map. SSIDs and portable suffixes are ignored, so adding N4ABC also covers N4ABC-7 and N4ABC/M.
readiness.head: READINESS
refdata.listsRefreshDaily: These lists refresh once a day on their own. Refreshing here downloads all of them now — useful after fixing whatever was blocking a download.
refdata.noListsReported: This node reported no reference lists.
refdata.someListsFailed: {ok} of {total} reference lists updated. Still failing: {lists}.
refdata.title: REFERENCE DATA
remoteAttachmentBlock.peerNotPairedEdge: peer not paired — this edge is dormant until re-paired
routingTable.dialedTgTypeName: dialed TG — type a name or number
routingTable.noOverridesEveryTalkgroup: No overrides — every talkgroup follows its network's prefix, and anything unrouted goes to the primary.
settings.chooseSection: Choose a section to configure this node.
settings.title: Settings
stackApplyNow.applyAvailableStackUpdates: Apply the available stack updates now? The affected services restart, and the update rolls back automatically if the modem does not come back up.
stackApplyNow.updateStartedHealthCheckin: Update started — health-checking the stack; this may take up to a minute.
startSweep.sweepingKeyRadioWhen: Sweeping — key your radio when it asks.
station.howLongNodeKeeps: How long this node keeps its persistent last-heard and event log (stored on-device). 0 keeps history forever. Older events are pruned nightly; a longer window uses more SD-card space.
station.idLine: Your node keys {callsign} in Morse every {minutes} minute(s) while idle, so it identifies itself without you touching it. Most licences require periodic identification — in the US, every 10 minutes (§97.119).
station.identificationSentBetweenTransmi: Identification is sent between transmissions, not during one.
station.nodeWillNotIdentify: This node will not identify itself. Automatic identification is off, so nothing announces your callsign on the air. Most licences require periodic identification — turn this on unless you are identifying by another means.
tab.brandmeister.desc: Master servers this node bridges DMR traffic to. Passwords are stored on the node and never shown.
tab.brandmeister.label: BrandMeister
tab.brandmeister.title: DMR Networks
tab.expert.label: Expert
tab.expert.title: Expert & System
tab.gateways.desc: Cross-mode routing is being redesigned as a bus system (RFC-0003).
tab.gateways.label: Gateways
tab.gateways.title: Cross-Mode Gateways
tab.general.desc: Station identity, operating frequencies and modem hardware for this hotspot node.
tab.general.label: General
tab.general.title: General Configuration
tab.hardware.desc: What modem is attached, what it says it is, and whether this node is configured to match. Detection asks the modem directly — it never guesses from the port it was found on.
tab.hardware.label: Hardware
tab.hardware.title: Modem Hardware
tab.lcd.desc: Drive a physical HD44780 character panel over I2C, with pages of live status that rotate. Disabled by default; the node stays headless until you turn it on.
tab.lcd.label: LCD
tab.lcd.title: LCD Display
tab.modes.desc: Which digital voice / data modes MMDVM-Host handles, and the per-mode settings behind each one. Toggling a mode restarts the stack on Apply.
tab.modes.label: Modes
tab.modes.title: Modes
tab.network.desc: Wireless credentials and IP configuration for the host device.
tab.network.label: Network
tab.network.title: Network & Wi-Fi
tab.notify.desc: Send email when something happens on this node — a text message arrives, an account is created, a weather alert goes out. Off by default. Addresses come from your Phonebook; anyone without one is simply not emailed.
tab.notify.label: Notifications
tab.notify.title: Notifications
tab.phonebook.desc: The operators this node knows: a callsign, optionally a DMR ID, and how to reach them. Nothing here changes what the radio does — entries are not part of your configuration, so adding one restarts nothing and needs no Apply.
tab.phonebook.label: Phonebook
tab.phonebook.title: Phonebook
tab.profiles.desc: Named snapshots of your mode & network setup — save the current one, switch to another in a click, or carry a setup between nodes as a file. Callsign, frequencies and calibration are never part of a profile, so switching can't change your identity or detune the radio.
tab.profiles.label: Profiles
tab.profiles.title: Connection Profiles
tab.publicview.desc: Publish a read-only page about this node — how to reach it, what it is for, and who has been heard. Off by default: until you enable it every public address answers "not found". Each field and module is controlled separately, and a suppress list keeps named callsigns out of everything published.
tab.publicview.label: Public View
tab.publicview.title: Public View
tab.setup.desc: TRX mode and the MMDVM-Host display driver. Waypoint runs display-free (status is served over MQTT); these fields are here for parity and for nodes driving a physical panel.
tab.setup.label: Setup
tab.setup.title: Control Software & Display
tab.station.desc: Node-wide operating policy: how long the persistent last-heard / event history is kept (pruned nightly), and how this node identifies itself on the air.
tab.station.label: Station
tab.station.title: Station Settings
tab.system.desc: The MQTT broker every daemon on this node shares, the topic roots it publishes under, and how much each daemon logs. These were start-up flags until now — changing them here takes effect on Apply.
tab.system.label: System
tab.system.title: System & Data Plane
tab.updates.desc: Installed versions, available updates from the signed Waypoint apt repo, and the update policy. Updates are applied on the node, health-checked, and rolled back automatically if the modem does not come back up.
tab.updates.label: Updates
tab.updates.title: Software Updates
tab.weather.desc: Broadcast National Weather Service alerts to your talkgroups as text and speech. Off by default; the node transmits nothing until you enable it and choose which counties and which hazards.
tab.weather.label: Weather
tab.weather.title: Weather Alerts
tgMapEditor.tgMapRewriteSource: TG map — rewrite a source-side talkgroup to a DMR TG (optional)
updates.allowUnrevertable: Allow updates that cannot be undone
updates.allowUnrevertableWarning: Updates that cannot be undone are allowed. If an update fails its health check, this node cannot go back to the versions it is running now, and will be left on the new ones. Turn this back OFF once the node is up to date.
updates.applyingStopsAffectedServices: Applying stops the affected services, installs the new versions, restarts, and health-checks the modem. If the stack does not come back up healthy it is automatically rolled back to the previous versions.
updates.applyingUpdateServicesAre: Applying an update… Services are being updated and health-checked. This page refreshes automatically.
updates.automaticUpdateChecksAre: Automatic update checks are off. This node checks only when you press CHECK NOW.
updates.automaticUpdateChecksAsk: Automatic update checks ask on a schedule whether a newer version exists. The request is an anonymous fetch of a signed, static file — it carries no callsign, no ID, and nothing else about this node, and there is no telemetry anywhere in Waypoint. Turn it OFF and the node stops asking on its own; CHECK NOW, applying an update, and everything else keep working — but automatic updates stop with it, since they install what a check found.
updates.defaultNotifyClickUpdates: Default is notify-and-click: updates wait for you to press UPDATE NOW. Turn Automatic updates ON to apply them during the quiet window (local time) instead.
updates.newWaypointdReleaseAvailable: A new waypointd release is available. Install it on the node with waypointd -update: the download is signature-verified before anything is touched, health-checked after the swap, and rolled back automatically if the new version does not come up.
updates.noCheckYet: No update check has run yet.
updates.signedAptRepoNot: The signed apt repo is not configured on this node, so stack updates are unavailable here. waypointd still self-updates its own binary (RFC-0014).
wx.addCountyCode: Add a county by SAME code
wx.addCountySearch: Search for a county by name or SAME code
wx.badSameCode: A SAME code is six digits, for example 012113.
wx.countiesNote: Pick counties by name; the six-digit SAME code a NOAA weather radio uses is stored for you. The list ships with this release and is searched on the node, so nothing about where you are leaves the device.
wx.countyShowing: {shown} of {total} shown — keep typing to narrow
wx.duplicateCounty: That county is already on the list.
wx.enabledNote: This transmits automatically, without anyone keying up. Everyone on the talkgroup receives it and cannot opt out, so choose the hazards below deliberately.
wx.feedNote: A free public feed of National Weather Service alerts. The default account is read-only and is published openly, so there is nothing to keep secret here.
wx.locationNote: Used only to suggest nearby counties. It is never published on the public page — the grid square shown there comes from the Public Page tab and nowhere else.
wx.noCounties: No counties yet. Alerts are matched by county, so nothing is broadcast until you add at least one.
wx.routingNote: A warning means the hazard is happening or imminent; a watch means conditions are favourable. Advisories and statements are the bulk of the feed and are off by default.
wx.talkgroupsNote: Separate several talkgroups with commas. Each one receives its own transmission. Receiving radios must have the talkgroup in their RX group list.
wx.testConfirm: This transmits a test message to your talkgroups. Everyone listening will hear it. Continue?
wx.testFailed: The test alert could not be sent.
wx.testNote: This transmits a clearly-marked test message to the talkgroups above, exactly as a real alert would. Everyone listening will hear it.
wx.timingNote: An alert waits for the channel to go quiet before it transmits. If it never does, the alert is dropped rather than sent on top of someone.
wx.toneNote: 1050 Hz is the tone NOAA weather radios use. It gets a listener's attention and nothing more — a DMR radio has no alert decoder, so no receiver will switch itself on for it.
wx.vocoder.none: None — spoken alerts will not transmit
wx.voiceNote: Speech needs a voice encoder that this node cannot supply on its own. With none selected, alerts are still sent as text and the spoken part is skipped and logged.
ysf.fcs00290YsfReflector: e.g. FCS00290 or a YSF reflector
ysf.gatewayBlockedFrequency: System Fusion is enabled but the radio frequencies are not set, so YSFGateway is not started — it builds its Wires-X service at startup and stops when either frequency is zero, which would leave the unit restarting in a loop. Set the receive and transmit frequencies on the General tab and apply. Nothing else about System Fusion is wrong. A DG-ID node is unaffected: DGIdGateway has no Wires-X, so turning DG-ID on also releases the gateway.
ysf.linkStartupReflectorDg: Link the startup reflector as a DG-ID network (YCS)
ysf.reflectorListNotLoaded: Reflector list not loaded yet (fetched from the YSF register on a schedule). You can still type a reflector id above.
ysf.uppercaseReflectorNamesHostlist: UPPERCASE reflector names in the hostlist
ysf.useDgidgatewayDgId: Use DGIdGateway (DG-ID addressed) instead of YSFGateway
ysf.wiresXPassthroughAdvanced: Wires-X passthrough (advanced — leave off for local control)
zello.accountStillUsed: This account is still used by a Zello channel. Remove the channel first.
zello.addAnAccountFirst: Add a Zello account before attaching a channel.
zello.asShownInApp: exactly as shown in the Zello app
zello.authTokenOptional: Token (only if you have no private key)
zello.dedicatedAccountNote: A node needs its own Zello account. Zello allows one session per account, so a node signed in as you signs you out of your phone, and signing back in signs the node out.
zello.mintsItsOwnTokens: This account signs its own tokens, so nothing expires.
zello.noAccountsYet: No Zello account yet. Add one to bridge a bus to a Zello channel.
zello.pastedTokenExpires: This account uses a pasted token, which stops working 30 days after it was issued and takes the bridge down without warning. Add the issuer and private key from developers.zello.com instead.
zello.storedLeaveBlank: stored — leave blank to keep it
